frequency_question: How often does an administrative review process result in formal revocation of an accrediting agency's status within a 24-month horizon?
membership_rule: Includes all federal reviews of institutional or programmatic accreditors initiated by petition or scheduled renewal where revocation or denial of recognition was formally considered and finalized by the Secretary of Education.

cases.name: American Bar Association (Prior NACIQI review deferred/renewed)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS)
American Career College (Initial petition denial/revocation context)

provenance_note: claims 60 cases from only 4 named (15.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 4 named key test cases detailed; approximately 56 routine renewals with full compliance or minor reporting requirements without formal revocation.
known_gaps: Does not separately isolate specialized programmatic accreditors from institutional accreditors, though both follow identical 34 CFR Part 602 procedural regulations.
skeleton: Total formal Secretary-level termination orders issued divided by total major periodic and compliance reviews of national/programmatic accreditors over the window.
multiplier: 2 revocations out of approximately 60 major agency reviews and renewals evaluated by NACIQI in the period.
validity_reason: The statutory and regulatory framework governing federal recognition of accreditors (Higher Education Act and 34 CFR Part 602) remains stable across multiple presidential administrations, changing only through deliberate negotiated rulemaking.
